title: Keep UVC webcams at a fixed frame rate
head: 500cb5aae8c4
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Already connected webcams are not configured when this rule first arrives in a settings-package upgrade
leads.consequence: On an existing install with a plugged-in UVC webcam, the new rule is only evaluated on a later add/change event. An omarchy-settings upgrade copies the rule but its scriptlet does not replay video4linux, and install/post-install/udev.sh triggers only power_supply. The camera therefore retains its current priority until a replug, reboot, or explicit video4linux trigger; a future event will apply the new setting. Suggest a scoped udevadm trigger --subsystem-match=video4linux after the package is installed, with a deliberate policy for not overwriting user-chosen settings on change events, or document the delayed effect.
leads.triage: dropped: documented intended behaviour (next boot or replug)

leads.summary: Rule needs companion package PR #664 for guaranteed v4l2-ctl and protected administrator overrides
leads.consequence: At the inspected package tip, neither settings package depends on v4l-utils nor lists etc/udev/rules.d/65-omarchy-webcam-framerate.rules in backup=(). The package copies all of etc/, so the file can ship without a guaranteed /usr/bin/v4l2-ctl and pacman can replace an edited rule on upgrade. The rule's '|| :' masks the missing binary as a successful RUN. The separate, currently open omarchy-pkgs#664 adds both entries for both package variants; coordinate the release/merge so neither package built from this head ships without #664. This is an integration dependency, not a defect remaining after #664 merges.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus (d); published as resolved via #664

leads.summary: The new test labels the rule package-owned without checking either packaging recipe
leads.consequence: The test's 'ships package-owned' check passes on source-tree presence only. At the inspected package tip it passes even though neither settings recipe guarantees /usr/bin/v4l2-ctl or backs up this /etc file, and test/shell.d/config-test.sh's package_defaults fixture does not include it. Add a focused recipe assertion for both settings variants (and update the fixture after companion #664) rather than claiming package ownership from -f alone.
leads.triage: dropped: config-test package_defaults does not list etc/udev rules by convention

leads.summary: Static RUN test passes even when the command only prints the requested control change
leads.consequence: Replacing /bin/sh -c '/usr/bin/v4l2-ctl ...' by /bin/sh -c 'echo /usr/bin/v4l2-ctl ...' produces twelve green assertions, including 'RUN calls v4l2-ctl' and 'RUN sets ... to 0', but executes echo instead of v4l2-ctl. The existing head has no echo; this is a concrete test-fidelity gap for a plausible debugging or wrapping mistake. Add an isolated RUN execution test using a fake v4l2-ctl to capture actual argv and status, or narrow the claim to static substrings. Actual sealed execution is in plan/runs/20260929T134053Z-82162310/output/mutant.out and a public-safe reproducer is reproducers/static-run-test-noop.md. Its udevadm verify is stubbed, so it does not demonstrate actual parser acceptance.
leads.triage: plausible from the test text; not published (contrived mutant)

leads.summary: On a v4l_id query failure, the rule silently skips a node rather than attempting the control
leads.consequence: 60-persistent-v4l invokes v4l_id; v4l_id prints ID_V4L_CAPABILITIES only when VIDIOC_QUERYCAP succeeds. An openable USB capture node whose QUERYCAP fails at that event has no capabilities property and never executes this rule; the user sees no warning. Whether any functional UVC webcam encounters this condition during add/change is unverified without a safe synthetic V4L device or actual device observations, so this is a hypothesis and not an established field regression.

limits: No physical camera or host udev execution permitted; video4linux and kernel event behavior was source-reviewed only. The isolated test run used a udevadm stub, not real udev verification.

flags.claim: Adding `|| true` to both makes the named check report, for example `not ok - the rule has a RUN key`.
flags.why: "the named check" implies the test then reports the missing rule itself. That holds only for the RUN-removed case, which prints `not ok - the rule has a RUN key`. With the rule line commented out and `|| true` added, the one-line check passes on the empty body (`wc -l <<<""` prints 1), and the first failure is `not ok - the rule runs on add and change`. A named `not ok` line does appear in both cases.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: 'makes a named check report instead'

flags.why: The reproducer is a text check. Its commands exit 0, and "fails" only means the printed line differs from the Expected line below it. Nothing in the block reports a failure status.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** At `500cb5a`, the added manual paragraph separates the resize lead-in from its hotkey table; the four points of the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13373#issuecomment-5851787218) are resolved.

| Earlier point | Status |
|---|---|
| `default=0` rationale | Resolved |
| Test skip and RUN snapshot | Resolved |
| Two-line comment-out trap | Resolved |
| `v4l-utils` dependency | Resolved in omacom/omarchy-pkgs#664 (open) |

### Manual paragraph splits the resize lead-in from its table

In `manual/12-screenshots-recording.md`, "resize it on the fly:" introduces the `Super + Alt + [` / `]` table. The new auto-exposure paragraph now sits between that colon and the table, so the colon introduces unrelated text.

**Suggested change:** move the paragraph below the table, after the `omarchy-capture-webcam-resize` sentence.

<details><summary>Reproducer (at 500cb5a)</summary>

Run from the repository root:

```bash
lead=$(grep -n 'resize it on the fly:$' manual/12-screenshots-recording.md | cut -d: -f1)
echo "lead-in line: $lead"
sed -n "${lead},$((lead+4))p" manual/12-screenshots-recording.md
```

Actual output:

```text
lead-in line: 53
When you record with a webcam, the camera appears as a pinned, cropped portrait window in the bottom-right corner of whatever you're recording. If it's sitting on top of something you need, resize it on the fly:

Omarchy also turns off the camera's auto-exposure priority when it's plugged in. UVC webcams commonly ship with it on, and in ordinary room light that quietly drops them to 10-15 fps while still reporting 30. The trade is a slightly darker picture in a dim room instead of a choppy one, the same trade browsers already make; a later-numbered udev rule can set `exposure_dynamic_framerate` back to 1 if you'd rather have the vendor behaviour.

| Hotkey | Function |
```

Expected: the line after the lead-in (after one blank line) is `| Hotkey | Function |`.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Earlier points**

- `default=0`: the description and commit message now call the 1 the vendor's power-on value. uvcvideo's AE-priority entry in `uvc_ctrls[]` still has no `UVC_CTRL_FLAG_GET_DEF` (Linux v7.2.8), so the corrected wording matches the driver.
- Test: the unavailable-`udevadm verify` branch now prints `# SKIP` with a reason, and the RUN is checked for its parts separately. The four mutation results in the author's reply reproduce: the numeric-ID form fails the by-name check, removing `|| :` fails the guard check, splitting the rule fails the one-line check, and reordering the arguments passes.
- Comment-out trap: match and RUN share one line. `udevadm verify` accepted the earlier two-line layout with only its match line commented out; commenting out the single line at this head disables the whole rule.
- `v4l-utils`: the reply said the dependency was left alone, but #664 was later updated to add `v4l-utils` to `depends` for `omarchy-settings` and `omarchy-settings-dev`, as the PR description now says.

**Verified**

- The PR test passes 12 of 12 in a sandbox, and `udevadm verify` accepts the rule.
- `*:capture:*` selects the same uvcvideo nodes as `:capture:`: uvcvideo capture nodes report exactly `:capture:` and metadata nodes `:`.
- No conflict with the current `quattro` tip.

**Optional notes**

- `change` also fires on package upgrades. On Arch, systemd's `35-systemd-udev-reload.hook` runs `udevadm trigger -c change` after any transaction that touches `usr/lib/udev/rules.d`, such as a systemd upgrade. The rule now re-runs then, so a value set by hand goes back to 0, and an override rule matching only `ACTION=="add"` is undone until the next replug or boot. Saying in the manual sentence that an override needs `ACTION=="add|change"` would prevent that. Source reading only; not run on a live system.
- When the rule line is commented out, or its RUN is removed on a host without `udevadm verify`, the test exits 1 with no named `not ok` line: the `rule_body=$(…)` and `run=$(…)` assignments fail under `set -euo pipefail` before any `fail` runs. Adding `|| true` to both makes a named check report instead, for example `not ok - the rule has a RUN key`.
- The manual's "the same trade browsers already make" is broader than the rule comment, which says Firefox never touches the control. "the same trade Chromium already makes" would match it.
</details>
